Though the hero is free to behave like a murderous sociopath during the game, completing the main quest will inevitably turn him into a big goddamn hero. Conversely, Fallout 1 allowed you to go with the Master's dream of turning everyone into super mutants, and although Fallout 2's ending inevitably ends with the destruction of the enclave (the "hero" ending), this does not prevent you from turning the wasteland into an even worse place than it already was.

Simply put: Fallout 3 is the result of Bethesda applying it's TES schematic on the Fallout setting. Yes, you can nuke Megaton, and you can secretly side with John Henry Eden by adding the FEV to the purifier, but at the end of the day you're still supposed to be "The Chosen One" by virtue of being Jame's child.

  1. As a general motion, RPGs become less and less RPG-y and more action-oriented.
